key_insight: Replace geometry-driven level-of-detail tokenization with a learned, semantics-aware hierarchy (LoST) so 3D shapes are represented with fewer, more meaningful tokens — improving token efficiency for autoregressive 3D generation.
problem_solved: State-of-the-art 3D tokenization uses spatial LoD hierarchies that are token-inefficient for AR generation; the paper addresses how to compress and structure 3D shape representations into compact, semantically meaningful tokens that better suit generative models.
method: Learn a multi-level semantic tokenization (Level of Semantics Tokenization) that groups geometry into semantically coherent units rather than purely spatial detail levels.
Construct a hierarchical codebook and encoding pipeline that produces fewer, higher-level tokens at coarse levels and finer semantic tokens only where needed.
Use the semantic token hierarchy as input to autoregressive generative models, improving generation quality and token-efficiency compared to geometric LoD baselines.
impact: LoST reduces token counts and yields more informative tokens for AR 3D generation, enabling more efficient training/inference and higher-quality outputs — useful for 3D content creation, compression, and downstream vision/graphics tasks.
visual_elements: Side-by-side schematic: geometric LoD tokenization vs semantic LoST tokenization highlighting token counts and what each token represents.
Pipeline diagram: input 3D shape → semantic encoder / hierarchical codebook → token hierarchy → autoregressive generator.
Bar chart: token-efficiency and generation quality comparison (tokens used vs reconstruction/generation metric) between LoD baselines and LoST.
Gallery: example reconstructions / generations showing crisper semantic parts (e.g., chairs, vehicles) produced with fewer tokens.
paper_title: LoST: Level of Semantics Tokenization for 3D Shapes
paper_authors: Niladri Shekhar Dutt, Zifan Shi, Paul Guerrero, Chun-Hao Paul Huang, Duygu Ceylan
